original_forecast.resolution_rule: Use the first U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation release for September 2026 published October 2, 2026 at 08:30 ET. Resolve TRUE if the first-published seasonally adjusted change in total nonfarm payroll employment is strictly below +100,000 jobs; otherwise FALSE. Score p=0.57 with Brier and log loss. Score the +90,000 point by absolute error against the same first-release payroll change and against the frozen +95,000 AP expectation and +162,000 prior-month no-change point. Record whether the first-release payroll change lies inside the -20,000 to +200,000 80% interval. Do not substitute later monthly revisions, benchmark revisions or post-cutoff consensus.
rationale: August JOLTS openings fell by 256K to 7.079M, providing a fresh gross labor-demand softening signal.
Hires remained near 5.2M and layoffs/discharges near 1.6M, so the model does not forecast a broad layoff-driven collapse.
September consumer expectations fell sharply, increasing downside risk to hiring, while low recent claims and August's +162K payroll print preserve upside uncertainty.

The point estimate is close to the contemporaneous external expectation rather than claiming a large consensus edge; the main test is whether the revised JOLTS-to-CES bridge avoids the prior P000025 magnitude error.
surprising_if: First-release payroll growth is at least +175,000.

resolution.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation — September 2026, first release published October 2, 2026 at 08:30 ET. Total nonfarm payroll employment changed by +29,000 and unemployment was 4.2%.
resolution.audit_note: Frozen original forecast preserved. The below-100K event resolved TRUE at +29K. p=0.57 beats neutral on this outcome but is only one observation. The +90K point missed by 61K, modestly beating the frozen +95K external expectation by 5K and materially beating the +162K prior-month no-change point. The -20K to +200K 80% interval covered. July and August were revised lower by a combined 60K, but those revisions do not alter the frozen target or scoring.
